This page holds the workshop's exercise, Tasks 1 to 5, on a copy of R that runs inside your browser, with the data already in place. It is the fallback when the slides do not load or an installation fails, and it gives the same numbers as the slides and the downloadable workspace.

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## While the R engine loads

The R engine downloads into your browser when you open this page (a minute or so, longer on a slow connection). It is ready when the first code cell shows a "Run Code" button. Your work is lost when the page is refreshed.
:::

<!--
The helpers of the browser lab, in one file included by three documents: the
lab itself, lab.qmd, and the two sets of web slides,
live/short.qmd and live/day.qmd, whose
hands-on slides run the same cells. The first cell holds the menu and the
helpers of Tasks 4 and 5, the second the graph functions of Task 2. The
including document sets .data_dir, the folder in which the files of its
resources list arrive inside the browser, in a setup cell placed before this
include, and lists among them the three files that the two cells read. The
estimator of the case study is written once, in R/_curve_tools.R;
these helpers fit no model and read every result from the curve, and the
graph functions read the answers of dagitty from a table.
-->


::: {.cell autorun='true'}
```{webr}
#| include: false
#| autorun: true
# The specification menu, its validation, and the helpers of Tasks 4 and 5:
# try_spec(), my_experiments(), submit_exploration(), prereg(), build_model(),
# run_spec() and report_result(). Every result is read from the curve of 864
# specifications in spec_curve.csv, and every option off the curve is refused
# with the reason recorded in menu_options.csv; both files arrive through the
# `resources:` list of the including page, in the folder .data_dir. No model is
# fitted here; the workspace fits the same specifications live, with their CR2
# test, and returns the same numbers.
.curve   <- utils::read.csv(file.path(.data_dir, "spec_curve.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
.options <- utils::read.csv(file.path(.data_dir, "menu_options.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                            encoding = "UTF-8")
.course_url <- "https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-eu"

# The thirteen axis codes that key the curve, in its column order; the
# inference rule is the fourteenth decision and is the same for every row.
.axis_codes <- c("outcome", "predictor", "copredictor", "estimator", "sample", "weights",
                 "construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form",
                 "family")
.neg_framings <- c("mcomm", "mlib", "mneg")

# The options that the curve keeps, in the three groups of the menu: the
# question, its measurement and the model. Every other option of the menu is
# listed in menu_options.csv.
.menu <- list(
  # The question
  my_outcome      = c("mcosmo", "mutil", "mpos"),
  my_predictor    = c("unemp", "growth"),
  my_copredictor  = c("none", "other"),
  my_estimator    = c("fe_twoway", "fe_country"),
  my_sample       = "all",
  my_weights      = "none",
  my_construction = "share",
  # Measurement
  my_noop         = c("zero", "drop"),
  my_item_set     = c("all", "un"),
  my_cell_weight  = c("unweighted", "design"),
  my_measure      = c("wb_nat", "es_1574_act", "es_2064_pop", "es_2564_lfs", "wb_growth"),
  # The model
  my_pred_form    = c("raw", "log"),
  my_family       = "gaussian",
  my_se           = "cr2"
)
.measures_for <- list(unemp  = c("wb_nat", "es_1574_act", "es_2064_pop", "es_2564_lfs"),
                      growth = "wb_growth")

if (nrow(.curve) != 864 ||
    !all(purrr::map_lgl(.axis_codes, \(a) all(.curve[[a]] %in% .menu[[paste0("my_", a)]]))))
  stop("The curve of 864 specifications did not load: reload the page.",
       call. = FALSE)
.curve_keys <- purrr::exec(paste, !!!unname(as.list(.curve[.axis_codes])), sep = "|")

.est_lab <- function(e) c(
  fe_twoway  = "two-way fixed effects (country + year)",
  fe_country = "country fixed effects")[[e]]
.se_lab <- "CR2 errors clustered by country, Satterthwaite df"

# The term for the claim-carrying predictor as it appears in a formula:
# log(unemp) when the log form is chosen, else the bare variable name.
.main_term <- function(ch) {
  if (ch$my_predictor == "unemp" && ch$my_pred_form == "log") "log(unemp)"
  else ch$my_predictor
}
.copred_term <- function(ch) if (identical(ch$my_predictor, "unemp")) "growth" else "unemp"

# --- validation ------------------------------------------------------------
# Two entry points into the same rules. .validate() takes a named list, which
# is how the exploratory try_spec() supplies its arguments; .check_choices()
# reads the fourteen my_* choices and claim_align out of the session, which is
# how the declared flow reads the preregistration cell. An option that is not
# on the curve stops with the reason from menu_options.csv, the
# workshop's page that teaches it, and the options that stay on the curve.
# A taught_on path may end in the id of a section, which the titles key and
# .page_ref() keeps in the address.
.page_titles <- c(
  "companion/measurement.qmd"      = "Scale construction",
  "companion/panel-data.qmd"       = "Panel data",
  "companion/dags.qmd"             = "Causal graphs",
  "companion/multiverse.qmd"       = "The multiverse and its critics",
  "companion/measurement.qmd#sec-noop"       = "Scale construction",
  "companion/measurement.qmd#sec-imputation" = "Scale construction",
  "companion/data-sources.qmd"     = "Social science data sources",
  "curve.qmd" = "Specification curve",
  "menu.qmd"  = "Specification menu",
  "menu.qmd#whose-average"  = "Specification menu",
  "menu.qmd#cell-weighting" = "Specification menu",
  "menu.qmd#outcome-family" = "Specification menu")
.page_ref <- function(path) {
  title <- if (path %in% names(.page_titles)) .page_titles[[path]] else path
  sprintf("%s, %s/%s", title, .course_url, sub(".qmd", ".html", path, fixed = TRUE))
}
.or_list <- function(x) {
  q <- paste0("\"", x, "\"")
  if (length(q) == 1) q else paste(paste(q[-length(q)], collapse = ", "), "or", q[length(q)])
}
# two older option codes that labels and calls may still use, mapped to the rows that hold their reasons
.legacy <- c("se:clustered" = "cr1", "weights:n_cy" = "n_cell")

.on_menu <- function(k, v) is.character(v) && length(v) == 1 && !is.na(v) && v %in% .menu[[k]]

.refuse <- function(k, v, ch, as_args) {
  shown <- function(a) if (as_args) a else paste0("my_", a)
  axis  <- sub("^my_", "", k)
  keep  <- if (k == "my_measure" && isTRUE(ch$my_predictor %in% names(.measures_for)))
    .measures_for[[ch$my_predictor]] else .menu[[k]]
  map   <- paste0("  Every decision and its options: ", .page_ref("menu.qmd"), "#map")
  if (!is.character(v) || length(v) != 1 || is.na(v))
    stop(sprintf("%s needs one option in quotes, for example %s = \"%s\".",
                 shown(axis), shown(axis), .menu[[k]][1]), call. = FALSE)
  look <- if (paste0(axis, ":", v) %in% names(.legacy)) .legacy[[paste0(axis, ":", v)]] else v
  row  <- .options[.options$axis == axis & .options$option == look & !.options$on_curve, ]
  msg <- if (nrow(row) == 1) c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" (%s) is not on the curve of 864 specifications.",
            shown(axis), v, row$label),
    paste0("  Why: ", row$reason),
    if (axis == "se")
      "  Inference is fixed: CR2 errors clustered by country, Satterthwaite df; the printout also gives the conventional t.",
    paste0("  Where it is taught: ", .page_ref(row$taught_on)),
    map,
    sprintf("  To stay on the curve, choose %s = %s.", shown(axis), .or_list(keep))
  ) else c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is not an option on the menu.", shown(axis), v),
    sprintf("  On the curve: %s.", paste(.menu[[k]], collapse = " | ")),
    if (any(.options$axis == axis & !.options$on_curve))
      sprintf("  Off the curve: %s.",
              paste(.options$option[.options$axis == axis & !.options$on_curve], collapse = " | ")),
    map
  )
  stop(paste(msg, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
}

.validate <- function(ch, as_args = FALSE) {
  shown <- function(a) if (as_args) a else paste0("my_", a)
  # the co-predictor may also be named by its variable, growth or unemp
  if (identical(ch$my_copredictor, .copred_term(ch)))
    ch <- utils::modifyList(ch, list(my_copredictor = "other"))
  bad <- purrr::discard(names(.menu), \(k) .on_menu(k, ch[[k]]))
  if (length(bad) > 0) .refuse(bad[1], ch[[bad[1]]], ch, as_args)
  if (ch$my_predictor == "growth" && ch$my_pred_form == "log")
    stop(sprintf("GDP growth takes negative values and enters raw only: use %s = \"raw\".",
                 shown("pred_form")), call. = FALSE)
  if (!ch$my_measure %in% .measures_for[[ch$my_predictor]])
    stop(sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is a series for %s; with %s = \"%s\" choose %s = %s.",
                 shown("measure"), ch$my_measure, setdiff(names(.measures_for), ch$my_predictor),
                 shown("predictor"), ch$my_predictor, shown("measure"),
                 .or_list(.measures_for[[ch$my_predictor]])), call. = FALSE)
  ch
}

.check_choices <- function() {
  need <- names(.menu)
  missing <- purrr::discard(need, \(k) exists(k))
  if (length(missing) > 0)
    stop("Not declared yet: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         ". Fill in every choice of the preregistration cell and run it.",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (!exists("claim_align"))
    stop("claim_align not declared: add claim_align <- TRUE to the preregistration cell.",
         call. = FALSE)
  .validate(purrr::set_names(purrr::map(need, \(k) get(k)), need))
}

# --- the curve -------------------------------------------------------------
.key_of <- function(ch) paste(unlist(ch[paste0("my_", .axis_codes)]), collapse = "|")

.lookup <- function(ch) {
  i <- match(.key_of(ch), .curve_keys)
  if (is.na(i))
    stop("The specification passed the checks but is not among the 864 on the curve: reload the page.",
         call. = FALSE)
  .curve[i, ]
}

# One result in the form that the printout and the submission use: the
# conventional fit (b, se, t, df, r), the claim-aligned r, the CR2 test with its
# Satterthwaite df, and the placement among the 864.
.result <- function(ch) {
  hit <- .lookup(ch)
  list(b = hit$b, se = hit$se, t = hit$t, df = hit$df, n = hit$n_cells, r = hit$r,
       r_ca = hit$r_ca, p_cr2 = hit$p_cr2, df_cr2 = hit$df_cr2,
       placement = mean(.curve$r_ca < hit$r_ca),
       source = "read from the curve of 864 specifications")
}

# The claim-alignment factor. The claim expects framing to rise with growth,
# so a growth slope is reported with its sign flipped; the negative framings,
# which are not on the curve, were reverse-coded the same way. The r_ca column
# of the curve is r times this factor.
.flip <- function(ch)
  (if (ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings) -1 else 1) *
  (if (ch$my_predictor == "growth") -1 else 1)

# The one-line spec label that the class chart reads: six of the seven
# decisions about the question, then in brackets the scoring rule, the
# measurement decisions and the decisions about the model, with the inference
# rule last.
.spec_line <- function(ch) {
  neg <- ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings
  paste0(ch$my_outcome, if (neg) "_ca" else "", " ~ ", ch$my_predictor, "(", ch$my_pred_form, ")",
         if (ch$my_copredictor == "other") paste0(" + ", .copred_term(ch)) else "",
         " | ", ch$my_estimator, " | ", ch$my_sample, " | w:", ch$my_weights,
         " [", ch$my_construction, ", ", ch$my_noop, ", items:", ch$my_item_set, ", cells:",
         ch$my_cell_weight, ", ", ch$my_measure, " | ", ch$my_family, ", se:", ch$my_se, "]")
}

# four decimals, so that a p just above 0.05 never prints as 0.050
.fmt_p <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else sprintf("= %.4f", p)

.class_line <- function(res) {
  below <- res$r_ca < 0
  sig   <- res$p_cr2 < 0.05
  if (below && sig) "below zero and significant under CR2 (p < 0.05), in the direction of the claim"
  else if (below) "below zero, but not significant under CR2 (p >= 0.05)"
  else if (sig) "above zero and significant under CR2, against the direction of the claim"
  else "above zero and not significant under CR2"
}

.print_result <- function(ch, res, lead = NULL, aligned = TRUE) {
  fl <- if (aligned) .flip(ch) else 1
  writeLines(c(
    lead,
    paste0("  ", .spec_line(ch)),
    sprintf("  b = %.5f   se = %.5f   t = %.3f on %d df (conventional standard error)",
            fl * res$b, res$se, fl * res$t, round(res$df)),
    sprintf("  partial r = %.3f, %s", if (aligned) res$r_ca else res$r,
            if (aligned) "claim-aligned (below zero is the direction of the claim)"
            else "on the original scale of the outcome"),
    sprintf("  p %s with CR2 errors clustered by country, on %.1f Satterthwaite df",
            .fmt_p(res$p_cr2), res$df_cr2),
    paste0(if (aligned) "  Class: " else "  Class, on the claim-aligned scale: ", .class_line(res)),
    sprintf("  Placement: %.0f%% of the 864 specifications on the curve have a more negative claim-aligned r",
            100 * res$placement),
    if (aligned && ch$my_predictor == "growth")
      "  (growth: b, t and r with their signs flipped, since the claim expects framing to rise with growth)",
    if (!aligned)
      "  (claim_align = FALSE: shown on the original scale; the class chart receives the claim-aligned values)",
    paste0("  (", res$source, ")")))
  invisible(res)
}

# --- Task 4: the exploratory helpers ---------------------------------------
.tried <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
assign("log", NULL, envir = .tried)
assign("last", NULL, envir = .tried)

try_spec <- function(outcome = "mcosmo", predictor = "unemp", copredictor = "none",
                     estimator = "fe_twoway", sample = "all", weights = "none",
                     construction = "share", noop = "zero", item_set = "all",
                     cell_weight = "unweighted", measure = NULL,
                     pred_form = "raw", family = "gaussian", se = "cr2") {
  if (is.null(measure)) measure <- if (identical(predictor, "growth")) "wb_growth" else "wb_nat"
  ch <- .validate(list(my_outcome = outcome, my_predictor = predictor, my_copredictor = copredictor,
                       my_estimator = estimator, my_sample = sample, my_weights = weights,
                       my_construction = construction, my_noop = noop, my_item_set = item_set,
                       my_cell_weight = cell_weight, my_measure = measure,
                       my_pred_form = pred_form, my_family = family, my_se = se), as_args = TRUE)
  res <- .result(ch)
  .print_result(ch, res, lead = "")
  fl  <- .flip(ch)
  row <- data.frame(stats::setNames(ch, sub("^my_", "", names(ch))),
                    b = fl * res$b, t = fl * res$t, r_aligned = res$r_ca, p_cr2 = res$p_cr2,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  assign("log", purrr::list_rbind(list(.tried$log, row)), envir = .tried)
  assign("last", list(ch = ch, res = res), envir = .tried)
  invisible(row)
}

# The running log of everything try_spec() has looked up. Only the decisions
# that varied are shown; the constant ones are those of the reproduced
# specification or of every call.
my_experiments <- function() {
  d <- .tried$log
  if (is.null(d)) {
    writeLines("Nothing tried yet: call try_spec() first.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  axes   <- sub("^my_", "", names(.menu))
  varied <- names(purrr::keep(d[axes], \(x) length(unique(x)) > 1))
  show <- d |>
    datawizard::data_select(select = c(varied, "b", "t", "r_aligned", "p_cr2")) |>
    datawizard::data_modify(b = signif(b, 3), t = round(t, 2), r_aligned = round(r_aligned, 3),
                            p_cr2 = round(p_cr2, 4))
  writeLines(sprintf("Specifications tried (%d):\n", nrow(d)))
  print(show, row.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(sprintf("\nSpread of claim-aligned r: %.3f to %.3f  |  below zero and significant under CR2: %d of %d",
                     min(d$r_aligned), max(d$r_aligned),
                     sum(d$r_aligned < 0 & d$p_cr2 < 0.05), nrow(d)))
  invisible(show)
}

submit_exploration <- function(nickname = NULL) {
  if (is.null(.tried$last))
    stop("Nothing to submit: call try_spec() first; the last specification tried is the one submitted.",
         call. = FALSE)
  .submit(.tried$last$ch, .tried$last$res, "explore",
          "Exploratory submission, claim-aligned (the last specification tried):",
          nickname)
}

# --- Task 5: the declared helpers ------------------------------------------

prereg <- function() {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  writeLines(c(
    "DECLARED – the preregistered specification, fixed before it is run:",
    "",
    "  The question",
    paste("    outcome    :", ch$my_outcome),
    paste0("    predictor  : ", ch$my_predictor,
           if (ch$my_predictor == "growth") " (sign flipped to align with the claim)"),
    paste("    adjusted   :", if (ch$my_copredictor == "other") .copred_term(ch) else "nothing"),
    paste("    estimator  :", .est_lab(ch$my_estimator)),
    paste("    sample     :", ch$my_sample, "   whose average:", ch$my_weights),
    paste("    scored as  :", ch$my_construction),
    "  Measurement",
    paste("    no-opinion rule:", ch$my_noop, "  items:", ch$my_item_set),
    paste("    cells:", ch$my_cell_weight, "  series:", ch$my_measure),
    "  The model",
    paste("    form:", ch$my_pred_form, "  family:", ch$my_family, "  inference:", .se_lab),
    paste("  claim_align:", isTRUE(claim_align)),
    "",
    "build_model(), run_spec() and report_result() read these choices."))
  invisible(ch)
}

build_model <- function(formula, estimator) {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  if (missing(formula) || !inherits(formula, "formula"))
    stop("The first argument must be a formula: outcome ~ predictor terms, unquoted.",
         call. = FALSE)
  lhs <- all.vars(formula[[2]])
  if (!identical(lhs, ch$my_outcome))
    stop(sprintf("The formula has the outcome '%s'; the preregistration declares '%s'. Change the formula to match.",
                 deparse(formula[[2]]), ch$my_outcome), call. = FALSE)
  want <- c(.main_term(ch), if (ch$my_copredictor == "other") .copred_term(ch))
  got  <- attr(terms(formula), "term.labels")
  if (!setequal(got, want))
    stop(sprintf("Right-hand side { %s } does not match the preregistered { %s }.%s",
                 paste(got, collapse = ", "), paste(want, collapse = ", "),
                 if (.main_term(ch) == "log(unemp)" && !"log(unemp)" %in% got)
                   " The preregistration declares the log form: write log(unemp)." else ""),
         call. = FALSE)
  if (missing(estimator) || !identical(estimator, ch$my_estimator))
    stop(sprintf("estimator = \"%s\" does not match the preregistered \"%s\".",
                 if (missing(estimator)) "" else estimator, ch$my_estimator), call. = FALSE)
  writeLines(c("Model accepted, matching the preregistration:",
               paste0("  ", deparse(formula), ", estimated by ", .est_lab(estimator)),
               "  Run it with run_spec(my_model)."))
  structure(list(choices = ch, formula = formula, estimator = estimator), class = "spec_ticket")
}

run_spec <- function(spec) {
  if (missing(spec) || !inherits(spec, "spec_ticket"))
    stop("Pass the object that build_model() returned, e.g. run_spec(my_model).", call. = FALSE)
  now <- .check_choices()
  if (!identical(spec$choices, now))
    stop("The preregistration cell has changed since build_model(): rerun prereg() and build_model().",
         call. = FALSE)
  ch  <- spec$choices
  res <- .result(ch)
  .print_result(ch, res, "Preregistered specification, read from the curve of 864:",
                aligned = isTRUE(claim_align))
}

# Both submissions of a participant carry one short tag inside the spec label,
# "explore: [amber-otter-42] …", so that the participant can find their own
# circles on the class chart. The tag rides in the free-text label because the
# form and its fields are frozen infrastructure. The same functions sit in
# R/spec_tools.R of the workspace, which keeps the tag in a file; here it lasts
# for the browser session, and a nickname passed to either submission function
# sets it or brings it back after a reload.
.tag_words <- list(
  adj  = c("amber", "azure", "bright", "calm", "coral", "crisp", "dusky", "early",
           "fair", "gentle", "golden", "hazel", "ivory", "jade", "keen", "lively",
           "lunar", "misty", "noble", "olive", "pale", "quiet", "rapid", "rosy",
           "russet", "silver", "snowy", "solar", "sunny", "swift", "velvet", "vivid"),
  noun = c("otter", "heron", "lynx", "badger", "finch", "hare", "ibex", "kestrel",
           "lark", "marten", "newt", "owl", "puffin", "quail", "raven", "seal",
           "stoat", "tern", "vole", "wren", "bison", "crane", "dove", "egret",
           "fox", "gecko", "koala", "lemur", "moose", "panda", "robin", "swan")
)
.tag_env <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
assign("tag", NULL, envir = .tag_env)

# A fresh tag, drawn without touching the random-number stream of the session.
.new_tag <- function() {
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)
  if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv())
  on.exit(if (had_seed) assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv())
          else rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()))
  set.seed(as.integer((as.numeric(Sys.time()) * 1000) %% 1e9) + Sys.getpid() %% 1e5)
  paste(sample(.tag_words$adj, 1), sample(.tag_words$noun, 1), sample(10:99, 1), sep = "-")
}

# A nickname reduced to lower-case ASCII letters, digits and single hyphens,
# at most 24 characters – the only form that the class chart parses.
.clean_tag <- function(x) {
  # iconv on Windows turns these into "?": the Romanian comma-below letters and the eszett
  x <- gsub("ß", "ss", chartr("ȘșȚț", "SsTt", trimws(as.character(x)[1])))
  ascii <- suppressWarnings(iconv(x, to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT"))
  if (!is.na(ascii)) x <- ascii
  x <- gsub("^-+|-+$", "", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(x)))
  x <- gsub("-+$", "", substr(x, 1, 24))
  if (is.na(x) || !nzchar(x))
    stop("A nickname needs at least one letter or digit, for example nickname = \"blue-heron\".",
         call. = FALSE)
  x
}

# The tag of this session: the nickname if one is given, otherwise the tag
# already drawn, otherwise a fresh one. Returns the tag and the one it replaced.
.class_tag <- function(nickname = NULL) {
  stored <- .tag_env$tag
  tag <- if (!is.null(nickname)) .clean_tag(nickname) else if (!is.null(stored)) stored else .new_tag()
  assign("tag", tag, envir = .tag_env)
  list(tag = tag, replaced = if (!is.null(stored) && !identical(tag, stored)) stored)
}

# One submission, used by both phases. The phase and the tag are prefixed to
# the free-text spec label, and all fourteen decisions are written into that
# label; the form, its fields and the collection pipeline are frozen
# infrastructure. The numbers are those of the conventional fit, claim-aligned.
.submit <- function(ch, res, phase, lead, nickname = NULL) {
  fl <- .flip(ch)
  b <- fl * res$b; tv <- fl * res$t; r <- res$r_ca
  tg <- .class_tag(nickname)
  spec_label <- paste0(phase, ": [", tg$tag, "] ", .spec_line(ch))

  FORM_ID <- "1FAIpQLSezoAEOnZUfP4pkfN28_XtEBwSyc2RLsXB-h8RPSegF7_t76A"
  field <- c(spec = "entry.832496914", b = "entry.1656311800", se = "entry.1337458262",
             t = "entry.1940779437", df = "entry.1682711955", n = "entry.1586392724",
             r = "entry.1660273001")
  value <- c(spec = spec_label, b = sprintf("%.5f", b),
             se = sprintf("%.5f", res$se), t = sprintf("%.3f", tv),
             df = as.character(round(res$df)), n = as.character(res$n),
             r = sprintf("%.3f", r))
  query <- names(field) |>
    purrr::map_chr(\(k) paste0(field[[k]], "=", utils::URLencode(value[[k]], reserved = TRUE))) |>
    paste(collapse = "&")
  url <- sprintf("https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/%s/viewform?usp=pp_url&%s", FORM_ID, query)

  writeLines(c(
    lead,
    "",
    paste("  spec:", spec_label),
    sprintf("  b = %.5f | se = %.5f | t = %.3f | df = %d | n = %d | r = %.3f",
            b, res$se, tv, round(res$df), res$n, r),
    paste0("  Class: ", .class_line(res)),
    "",
    "Open the address below and press Send: every field of the form is filled in.",
    "",
    url))
  writeLines(c(
    "",
    sprintf("Tag on the class chart: %s%s.", tg$tag,
            if (!is.null(tg$replaced)) sprintf(" (replaces %s)", tg$replaced) else ""),
    sprintf("Typed into the my_tag line of %s/class-results.html, it highlights your marks.", .course_url),
    sprintf("Both submissions carry it until the page reloads; after a reload, pass nickname = \"%s\".", tg$tag),
    "To choose another, pass nickname = \"...\" (a nickname, not your name: the chart is public)."))
  invisible(list(spec = spec_label, tag = tg$tag, b = b, se = res$se, statistic = tv,
                 df = res$df, n = res$n, r = r, url = url))
}
```

```{webr}
  "No stored answer for this graph. The page holds the adjustment sets of the graph",
  "of the cell with any of its commented arrows switched on; for any other graph,",
  "use dagitty in the workspace (R/dag_starter.R).")

# A graph from one formula per arrow. coords is accepted, as ggdag::dagify()
# accepts it, and not used, because this page does not draw the graph. The
# arrows, sorted, are the key under which data/dag_answers.csv holds the
# answers for the graph.
dagify <- function(..., exposure = NULL, outcome = NULL, coords = NULL) {
  e <- purrr::map(list(...), \(f) {
    child <- all.vars(f[[2]])
    parent <- all.vars(f[[3]])
    data.frame(from = parent, to = rep(child, length(parent)))
  }) |>
    purrr::list_rbind()
  structure(list(edges = e, exposure = exposure, outcome = outcome,
                 nodes = unique(c(e$from, e$to)),
                 key = paste(sort(unique(paste(e$from, "->", e$to)), method = "radix"),
                             collapse = "; ")),
            class = "simple_dag")
}

# The minimal adjustment sets for the total effect of the exposure on the
# outcome, as dagitty::adjustmentSets() returns them, read from the table
adjustmentSets <- function(x, exposure = x$exposure, outcome = x$outcome, effect = "total", ...) {
  rows <- .dag_answers[.dag_answers$arrows %in% x$key &
                         .dag_answers$exposure %in% paste(exposure, collapse = ", ") &
                         .dag_answers$outcome %in% paste(outcome, collapse = ", ") &
                         .dag_answers$effect %in% effect, ]
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) {
    writeLines(.dag_elsewhere)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  structure(strsplit(rows$answer[rows$item > 0], ", ", fixed = TRUE), class = "simple_dag_sets")
}

print.simple_dag_sets <- function(x, ...) {
  if (!length(x)) {
    writeLines("(no set of these variables closes every backdoor path)")
  } else {
    purrr::map_chr(x, \(z) if (length(z)) paste0("{ ", paste(z, collapse = ", "), " }") else "{}") |>
      writeLines()
  }
  invisible(x)
}

# Registered rather than left in the session: these cells do not evaluate in
# the global environment, so plain S3 dispatch would not find the method.
registerS3method("print", "simple_dag_sets", print.simple_dag_sets)
```

## Warm-up – the three Rs {#task-1-concepts-warm-up-while-the-engine-loads}

Three of the four scenarios below describe one of the three Rs (reproducibility, robustness, replicability), and the fourth describes something else. Read all four, then fill in the gaps in the code cell and run it.

***Scenario 1:*** A reviewer reruns the authors' Stata .do file on the authors' data and gets a *different* coefficient from the one printed in the paper. This is an example of \_\_\_\_\_\_ even though what they *tried* to do failed.

***Scenario 2:*** The analyst uses the authors' submitted replication dataset, but they re-implement the model in R instead of Stata and centre the predictor. Is this a case of  \_\_\_\_\_\_ or \_\_\_\_\_\_?

***Scenario 3:*** A preregistered team tests the identical hypothesis on a *separate, much larger* dataset chosen to be theoretically equivalent, and gets results that contradict the original. Their conclusion is that the original analysis has failed to \_\_\_\_\_\_.

***Scenario 4:*** Instead of the survey data used by the original authors, another researcher tests the same underlying idea on social-media texts using a machine-learning classifier method that the original never used. To their surprise, the authors' original findings turn out to be \_\_\_\_\_\_, and the researcher concludes that they provide a reliable middle-range theory of the phenomenon they investigate.

```{webr}
  "Scenario 1: This is an example of ______.",
```

## Answers

1.  **reproducibility** – rerunning the same code on the same data. Here it *failed* to match, but the activity is still reproducibility, and 'not reproduced' is the verdict.
2.  arguably still **reproducibility**, in a grey area – re-implementing on the same data in different software is technically a re-computation – but centring the predictor nudges towards **robustness**. Two packages can also implement the same estimator differently, so make sure you know what the function you call is doing.
3.  **replicability** – same question, independent new data chosen to be theoretically equivalent.
4.  **generalisability** – the odd one out, with new data *and* a new method at once. It is the fourth cell of the matrix, outside the three that the exercise tests.

## Task 2, continued – the estimand and the graph {#task-4-estimand-and-dag}

Before fitting anything, say what you are trying to estimate, in words. A template you can adapt:

> The **unit-specific quantity** is the change in mean cosmopolitan EU framing within a country from one year to another associated with a one-point change in that country's unemployment rate. The **target population** is EU member states over 2004–2013. The **aggregation** is a weighted average of those unit-specific effects, in which the country-years whose unemployment departs most from their country and year means count most, holding fixed each country's time-invariant traits and each year's EU-wide shocks.

That last clause is a causal claim, and a directed acyclic graph (DAG), a diagram in which arrows run from cause to effect, makes it checkable, as the [module on causal graphs](companion/dags.qmd#sec-arrows) explains. The graph below draws the five arrows that this exercise takes as given, which the rest of this page calls the committed arrows, and further down you decide which of the arguable arrows to add to them.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![The committed graph: unemployment to framing, with country and year each a common cause of both. The three pale nodes have no arrows yet.](lab_files/figure-html/dag-reference-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768}
:::
:::


`unemployment -> framing` is the path of interest. `country` is a common cause of both: stable national traits such as size, EU tenure and labour-market institutions move local unemployment and shape how people frame the EU. `year` does the same job for the EU-wide shocks that hit every country in the same calendar year. The three pale nodes below have no arrows yet, because whether they belong is your decision.

You build the graph yourself in the cell below. `dagify()` takes one formula for each arrow, written the way you write a model, so `framing ~ unemployment` is the arrow that runs *into* `framing`: read the tilde as 'is caused by' rather than 'is regressed on'. The five committed arrows are live, and the arguable ones are commented out, one substantive claim per line. Uncomment any that you believe, then run the cell, which stores the graph as `my_dag`.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
my_dag <- dagify(
  # The path of interest, and the two common causes (country and year)
  # that two-way fixed effects absorb.
  framing      ~ unemployment,
  framing      ~ country,
  unemployment ~ country,
  framing      ~ year,
  unemployment ~ year,

  # GROWTH as a time-varying confounder: a slump raises unemployment and may
  # sour EU sentiment in the same year.
  # framing      ~ growth,
  # unemployment ~ growth,

  # BAILOUT as a mediator: unemployment triggers a financial-assistance
  # programme, which then shapes framing.
  # bailout ~ unemployment,
  # framing ~ bailout,

  # POLITICISATION of the EU by parties and elites as another cause of
  # framing. The robustness study instructed analysts to disregard it.
  # framing ~ politicisation,

  exposure = "unemployment",
  outcome  = "framing",
  # Coordinates of all seven nodes; those of a node that no arrow names are
  # ignored.
  coords = list(
    x = c(unemployment = 0, framing = 3, country = 1, year = 2,
          growth = 0.9, bailout = 1.5, politicisation = 3),
    y = c(unemployment = 0, framing = 0, country = 1.4, year = 1.4,
          growth = -1.0, bailout = -1.2, politicisation = -0.95)))
```
:::


Then ask for the adjustment set of the graph that you have just written. On this page `adjustmentSets()` prints the answer that dagitty, the R package for causal graphs, gave for every combination of the arrows in the cell ([codebook](data/dag_answers_codebook.md)), and any other graph gets a pointer to the workspace, where dagitty itself runs.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
adjustmentSets(my_dag)
```
:::


With the five committed arrows the minimal adjustment set is `{ country, year }`, which is what a two-way fixed-effects model absorbs. An adjustment set is a set of variables that, once adjusted for, blocks every non-causal path from unemployment to framing, and it is minimal when no variable can be dropped from it without reopening one of those paths. The two-way fixed-effects model of analyst C6HJR, one of the three that you can reproduce in Task 3, therefore makes the same identification claim as the graph you have just written, while the model of KQXUE adjusts for the country alone and the random intercepts of 018OL adjust for neither in this sense.

Now uncomment the growth pair and run the two cells again. The set becomes `{ country, growth, year }`, because a slump varies within a country over time and fixed effects remove only country-constant and year-common variation, so a specification that matches your beliefs would need `growth` as a co-predictor, a choice that the adjustment-set decision of the menu offers in Task 5. The bailout arrows behave differently: a mediator lies on the path you are trying to measure, so the adjustment set does not grow when you add one, and adjusting for it would remove part of the effect that you are trying to estimate.

Write two sentences for your own notes. What do two-way fixed effects adjust for, and what can they **not** fix? (Hint: anything time-varying within a country that you have not measured.)

## Hint – the random intercepts and the degrees of freedom

Each `(1 | x)` gives the cells that share a value of `x` an intercept of their own, so the missing one is `(1 | year)`. `parameters::model_parameters()` reports the degrees of freedom that `ci_method` names, and `lmerTest` provides the Satterthwaite approximation, `ci_method = "satterthwaite"`.
:::
::::

:::: {.solution exercise="reproduce-018ol"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Fully worked solution

``` r
m3 <- lmerTest::lmer(pos01 ~ unemp + (1 | cntry) + (1 | year) + (1 | wave), data = o18ol)
print(parameters::model_parameters(m3, effects = "fixed", ci_method = "satterthwaite"), digits = 5)
```

You should get a coefficient of −0.00203, a standard error of 0.00169 and t = −1.20627 on 396.92 degrees of freedom, the −1.206 on record. The year in the file is the one that 018OL took from the names of its data files, which put the wave EB 79.3, fielded in 2013, in 2012; the column `year_fieldwork` holds the true year. A rebuild that dates every wave by its fieldwork, and so merges the unemployment of 2013 onto those cells, gives t = −1.606 instead, so a rebuild that dates the waves correctly does not recover the recorded value.
:::
::::

## Task 5 – Preregistration {#task-5-my-preregistration}

Preregistration means setting out your choice in a plan **before** you know what it does, which stops you from quietly picking the specification that happens to give the answer you wanted. On this page the plan is the cell below: every later cell reads your choices from it, and `build_model()` refuses code that departs from them. Its numbered fields follow the preregistration template of AsPredicted in a shortened form, and field 2 also stands in for the prior-knowledge section of the template for secondary data (van den Akker et al. 2021).

Make one choice on each decision of the [specification menu](menu.qmd), complete the dotted lines, then run the cell. `claim_align <- TRUE` is the workshop's convention, applied automatically: the claim expects framing to rise with GDP growth, so the sign of a growth slope is flipped, and 'supports the claim' reads as a negative sign for everyone.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# ============================================================================
# MY PREREGISTRATION – one specification, declared before seeing its result
# ============================================================================
# 1. The claim I am testing: .................................................
# 2. The data + what I already know: europeanisation_cy.csv (270 country-years,
#    public); I know that the reproduced specification gives t = -3.804,
#    and what my exploration in Task 4 showed.
# 3. My one specification – one choice on each decision. An option that is
#    not on the curve of 864 stops prereg() with the reason why.

# The question (each of these changes what is being estimated)
my_outcome      <- "mcosmo"       # mcosmo | mutil | mpos   (the positive framings)
my_predictor    <- "unemp"        # unemp | growth    (the measure whose coefficient tests the claim)
my_copredictor  <- "none"         # none | other      (the other economic measure, adjusted for)
my_estimator    <- "fe_twoway"    # fe_twoway | fe_country
my_sample       <- "all"          # all    (the 27 member states, 2004–2013)
my_weights      <- "none"         # none   (every country-year counts once)
my_construction <- "share"        # share  (the share of a respondent's own mentions)

# Measurement (the same question, put to the data differently)
my_noop         <- "zero"         # zero | drop   (respondents who mentioned no frame at all)
my_item_set     <- "all"          # all | un   (with or without the "unemployment" item)
my_cell_weight  <- "unweighted"   # unweighted | design   (cells as interviewed, or weighted)
my_measure      <- "wb_nat"       # unemp:  wb_nat | es_1574_act | es_2064_pop | es_2564_lfs
                                  # growth: wb_growth

# The model (the same question and measures, another fit)
my_pred_form    <- "raw"          # raw | log   (growth: raw only; centring or z-scaling
                                  #              would leave t, r and p unchanged)
my_family       <- "gaussian"     # gaussian   (a linear model of the cell means)
my_se           <- "cr2"          # cr2   (fixed: CR2 errors clustered by country)

claim_align     <- TRUE           # the workshop's convention, applied automatically

# 4. Why these controls, in one DAG-grounded sentence: .......................
# 5. Supported if the claim-aligned coefficient is negative with CR2
#    p < .05; undermined if it is not significant or positive. I will
#    report what I get.
```
:::


Then run `prereg()`, which checks every choice against the menu and prints your preregistration.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
prereg()
```
:::


The preregistration cell, copied into your notes, is your preregistration record.



## Task 5, continued – build, run and report {#task-5-build-run-report}

Translate your declared specification into model syntax yourself, filling the three gaps (the outcome, the right-hand side and the estimator code) as you preregistered them. `build_model()` reads your declaration and accepts nothing else, and its error messages tell you what is off. Write the log form as `log(unemp)`, and add any co-predictor with `+`.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
my_model <- build_model(______ ~ ______, estimator = "______")
```
:::


::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Hint – from menu speak to model syntax

The formula uses the column names of `europeanisation`, with the outcome that you preregistered on the left of `~` and the predictor terms on the right. For a declaration of the reproduced specification it is `mcosmo ~ unemp`. With the log form it would be `mcosmo ~ log(unemp)`, and with a co-predictor `mcosmo ~ unemp + growth`. The estimator is the menu code itself, in quotes: `"fe_twoway"` or `"fe_country"`. You do not write the fixed-effects syntax here – the estimator code stands for it, and the cells of C6HJR and KQXUE in Task 3 showed what it expands to. Apart from the log form, the measurement decisions and the decisions about the model never appear in the formula. They select which version of the panel the result was computed on.
:::

When the model is accepted, run it. Every specification on the curve is pre-computed: the page loaded the results of all 864 with the data, and `run_spec()` picks the one that matches your declaration, with the numbers that the downloadable workspace gives when it fits the model on your own machine:


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
run_spec(my_model)
```
:::


The output has the same lines as in Task 4, and the placement is the share of the 864 specifications on the curve that lie further in the direction of the claim than yours, 67% for the reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR in Task 3.

Now send it to the class chart. The cell prints your submission line and the address of a pre-filled form. Open the address and press **Send**. Your dot joins the live [class chart]({{< var live-results-url >}}) within seconds, labelled **declared**, with the same tag as your exploratory result. If you have reloaded this page since Task 4, pass the tag back with `report_result(nickname = "your-tag")`.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
report_result()
```
:::


If the form will not open on your machine, read the printed numbers to the facilitator, who adds your dot to the chart.

A second declaration is possible: edit the preregistration cell, rerun `prereg()`, rebuild and rerun. The chart still labels it declared, but it was chosen after a result was known, as the specifications of Task 4 were, so say so wherever you write about the result.
